title: Fresh 'hi' returns a greeting only, never the menu

expected.notes: Locks the greeting-must-never-trigger-menu regression: a bare greeting must never be expanded into the full priced menu, even if the model's own draft politely offers to show it.

title: Fresh 'hello' returns a greeting only, never the menu

expected.notes: Same rule as greeting-hi-fresh, different exact greeting word.

title: Fresh 'hey' returns a greeting only, never the menu

expected.notes: Same rule as greeting-hi-fresh, different exact greeting word.

title: Fresh 'salam' returns a greeting only, never the menu

expected.notes: Roman Urdu greeting variant — same rule as greeting-hi-fresh.

title: Fresh 'assalam o alaikum' returns a greeting only, never the menu

expected.notes: Full formal greeting variant — same rule as greeting-hi-fresh.

title: 'hello there' (English, not an exact single-word greeting) is still handled politely
messages: hello there, is this Think Food?

expected.notes: A longer greeting-shaped message should still be answered as a greeting/identity confirmation, not dumped into the menu.

title: 'hi' then a separate explicit 'menu' request shows the menu on the SECOND turn only

expected.notes: Proves the greeting exclusion doesn't also block a genuinely explicit menu request made afterward in the same conversation.

title: 'hi, menu dikhao' (greeting + explicit ask in ONE message) still gets the menu

expected.notes: The greeting exclusion is an exact whole-message match, never a substring — a message that merely opens with a greeting word but also contains a real request must not be blocked from its real content.

title: A greeting never mutates the cart

expected.notes: A greeting carries no item mention at all, so nothing should ever land in the cart from it.

title: Two greetings in a row both stay greetings, never escalate to the menu

expected.notes: Repeating a greeting must not eventually 'fall through' to a menu dump on a later turn.
